definition: In Jaimini astrology, the planet with the highest degree within its sign among the planets included in the chosen chara-karaka scheme. It represents a central life lesson and inner direction.
In KP astrology, the planet ruling the subdivision containing a house cusp. Its house connections help assess whether that house can deliver the event being examined.
Krishnamurti Paddhati: an astrology method using house cusps, nakshatra rulers and sub-lords to assess events and their timing.
The main birth chart, calculated for the birth time and place. It provides the basic planetary, sign and house placements used to interpret the other charts.
The zodiac point rising on the eastern horizon at birth. It establishes the first-house reference and the orientation of the birth chart.
The planet ruling the ascendant sign. Its position and condition connect the person and their overall life direction with the houses it influences.
The tenth divisional chart, used to refine career, responsibility and professional achievement shown in the main birth chart.
The twenty-fourth divisional chart, traditionally examined for education, scholarship and learning. It refines the birth-chart promise and is sensitive to birth-time accuracy.
The approach associated with Parashara, using planetary placements, house rulerships, aspects, strengths and dashas to interpret a chart.
The approach associated with Jaimini, using chara karakas, sign-based relationships, arudhas and sign dashas as interpretive tools.
A family of astrological traditions. In this app, Nadi analysis examines planetary connections and sequences to relate different life themes.
A perspective that compares houses from the ascendant, Moon and Sun to examine the same life topic from three reference points.
An astrological timing period ruled by a planet or sign. A dasha indicates which existing chart themes may become active during that period.
A 120-year planetary dasha cycle based on the Moon’s birth nakshatra, subdivided into successively shorter periods.
The main planetary period in a dasha system. Its planet sets the broad themes of that stage of life.
A sub-period within a mahadasha. Its planet works with the main-period ruler to refine the themes and timing.
A sub-period within an antardasha, used to examine a shorter timing window.
A Jaimini sign-based timing system. Each zodiac sign becomes the reference for a period, interpreted using its planetary and house connections.
A traditional measure of a planet’s capacity to give difficult or frustrating results. It is interpreted alongside strength, house rulership and active timing.
A zodiac sign ruled by the planet placed in it. This is a dignity condition that supports the planet’s capacity, while the outcome still depends on its role in the chart.
A particularly supportive sign region for a planet, traditionally distinguished from its ordinary own-sign placement. It describes dignity rather than a guaranteed outcome.
A planet or influence considered supportive in an astrological context. Natural benefic status and a planet’s functional role for a particular ascendant are separate considerations.
A planet considered constructive because of the houses it rules for the particular ascendant. This role can differ from its natural benefic or malefic classification.
A calculated point derived from the Sun and Moon. Its nakshatra ruler is the Yogi planet, a special indicator of supportive potential.

The nakshatra ruler of a point offset from the Yogi point, traditionally examined for obstruction. In this app, its contribution is assessed with placement, aspects and cancellation or reversal rules.
In this app’s Avayogi rule, houses 3, 6, 8 and 12 can reverse the Avayogi contribution from obstructive to supportive. This changes only that contribution, not other difficult chart factors.
Zodiac signs classified as dagdha, or burnt, from the birth lunar day under the selected traditional rule. These are additional constraints, interpreted with the full chart.
The boundary or reference point used to define an astrological house. The specific definition depends on the house system; KP interprets the cusp’s sign, star and subdivisions.
The planet ruling the nakshatra occupied by a planet or cusp. In KP, that ruler’s house connections contribute to the significations.
In KP, the ruler of the proportional subdivision of a nakshatra containing a planet or cusp. It refines how the associated house themes are interpreted.
In KP, the ruler of a further subdivision within a sub-lord segment, used for finer distinctions and timing.
A KP-related method that evaluates a planet and its stellar and subdivision connections to identify relevant houses. The exact four-step convention should be stated because implementations differ.
A planet’s or cusp’s connection with houses and their life themes through placement, rulership and the rules of the selected astrology method.
A relationship through which a planet or sign is considered to influence another chart location. Aspect rules differ between Parashari, Jaimini and other methods.
A relationship between placements roughly 180 degrees apart. Its astrological meaning depends on the method and the specific planets involved.
A nakshatra in Cancer, ruled by Saturn in Vimshottari timing and associated traditionally with nourishment, support and growth. Its meaning depends on the planet occupying it.
A nakshatra spanning late Sagittarius and early Capricorn, ruled by the Sun in Vimshottari timing. Its traditional themes include enduring achievement and responsibility.
A traditional nakshatra classification associated with stable or enduring activities in electional astrology. It does not mean every planet placed there produces an unchanging life outcome.
The collective deities traditionally associated with Uttara Ashadha. Their symbolism is used as one interpretive layer of that nakshatra.
One of the 27 lunar mansions used in Vedic astrology. It adds a finer positional and interpretive layer and helps determine several timing systems.
One of the four quarters of a nakshatra, used to refine its subdivision and divisional connection.
The current movement of planets relative to the birth chart, used to examine activation and timing of chart themes.
A chart formed by subdividing zodiac signs under a specified rule. It refines a particular life topic and should be read alongside the main birth chart.
